problem: Existing ObjectNav agents only imitate coordinate trajectories, so they cannot explain their decisions or plan hierarchically (room, then furniture, then object). In long-horizon navigation they also keep redundant history from revisited areas and loop over the same paths.
motivation: Agents need perception, planning and prediction to navigate unseen scenes reliably. Standard navigation data has no perception or planning supervision, and dense history is costly and redundant: the paper shows near-identical views at T=71, 82 and 90. Jointly training with EQA data and pruning redundant history should improve long-term navigation.
key_idea: Jointly train an LLM-based navigation agent on navigation and GPT-4o-generated EQA data (scene perception, path planning, commonsense) and feed it a position-enhanced, redundancy-pruned history chosen by an adaptive 3D-aware sampling rule.
insight: Both components help in ablation on ObjectNavRoom. Adding EQA joint training raises SR 42.5 to 47.2 and SEL 16.0 to 21.9. On full ObjectNav, SR rises 72.5 to 81.1, so more EQA data yields larger gains. Removing history sampling costs 2.2 SR and removing position encoding costs 2.9 SR, and hyper-parameters matter: too long a window (W>60) or too sparse/dense sampling hurts.
method: Visual encoder: CLIP ViT gives 2D features X_t, and UVFormer with learnable queries and camera parameters gives 3D tokens UV_t (400 tokens, trained with an occupancy loss).

Adaptive 3D-aware history sampling: scan history from newest to oldest, skip a frame if it lies within distance epsilon and has cosine similarity above tau to an already selected frame, stop at window W, and pad with the last valid frame; each frame is max-pooled to 1 token.
Position-enhanced historical features: sinusoidal 2D encoding of the relative (x,y) position is added to history features, followed by an FC layer.
LLM (MPT-1B) with two heads: an MLP action head for navigation and an LM head for EQA answers; the self-attention layers are frozen and the cross-attention layers are fine-tuned.

EQA dataset construction: GPT-4o receives an instruction-centric prompt (role and two exemplars) plus the final W frames of each trajectory, and generates a scene description, path plan and commonsense reasoning (99k pairs for CHORES-S, 21k for ObjectNavRoom).
Multitask collaboration: joint loss L = L_action (behavior-cloning CE) + L_answer (token CE) + lambda*L_occ; inference uses navigation actions only.

setting.backbone: CLIP ViT + UVFormer + MPT-1B LLM (cross-attention fine-tuned, self-attention frozen)
setting.training_data: CHORES-S ObjectNav: 99k expert trajectories (5M frames, 10k houses) plus 99k GPT-4o-generated EQA pairs; ObjectNavRoom ablation: 21k trajectories plus 21k EQA pairs
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (wrist camera for navigation, head camera for EQA) with camera parameters and agent position history
setting.action_space: 20 discrete low-level mobile-manipulator actions (move base ±20 cm, rotate base ±6°/±30°, arm moves, grasper rotation, pickup, dropoff, done, terminate)
setting.privileged: none stated (agent absolute positions from odometry are used for history sampling)

numbers.extra: joint training with 99k GPT-4o EQA pairs; W=60, eps=0.1, tau=0.95; best checkpoint chosen by SR on the evaluation split
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Performance comparison on CHORES-S ObjectNav benchmark; official evaluation split of 200 trajectories in 200 houses

numbers.extra: ablation benchmark trained on 21k trajectories plus 21k EQA pairs

numbers_note: The split for the ObjectNavRoom ablation is not named explicitly (labeled 'val' as an evaluation split). The main result is on the official CHORES-S evaluation split.
results: RoboTron-Nav reaches 81.1 SR on CHORES-S ObjectNav, beating RING (72.1) and SPOC* (60.0) by about 9 points absolute, with 67.8 %Rooms. Its SEL (43.9) is lower than RING (53.0) and SPOC (46.2).
limitations: SEL is lower than RING and SPOC, so paths are less efficient despite higher success.
Evaluated only in simulation on one benchmark (CHORES-S); the ablations use the smaller ObjectNavRoom, and multitask training takes about twice as long.
Depends on GPT-4o-generated EQA data, and checkpoints are selected by SR on the evaluation split.
